name: Finland
headline: Finland: +0.8% growth in 2025, 1.8% inflation, debt 88% of GDP
sections: Finland is a $318 billion economy (2025), the world's 49th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +0.8% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $66K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 14.2% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 1.8% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 7.2% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 9.7% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 21.5% (2025).
Gross government debt is 88% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has risen from 75% in 2020. The general government balance is −3.8% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is +1.0% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 83% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 0.1% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 101% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 82.3 years (2024). Population: 5.6 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
